page: Microsoft Azure D48_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor. This server provides 48 vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It also comes bundled with 1229 GB of local SSD storage, while lacking any dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile characterized by average multi-core capabilities but weak single-core execution. The single-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench falls into the bottom 10%, reflecting the older architecture and moderate clock speed of the Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4. However, the 48 vCPUs deliver average multi-core performance in stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth and database operations also perform in the middle 50% tier, though text processing and LLM text generation tasks show weaker results, with text generation falling into the bottom 10%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D48_v3 offers a high resource density of vCPUs and memory on legacy hardware, making it a viable option for workloads that benefit from parallel execution rather than raw single-threaded speed. The bundled 1229 GB SSD provides substantial local storage capacity without requiring external attachments. This configuration is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, general-purpose web serving, database operations, and software compilation, whereas it is less suitable for single-threaded tasks or real-time LLM text generation.
